statement: For a holomorphically embedded pointed disc $(D,p)$ in a Riemann surface $Y$, choose a biholomorphism $f:\D\to D^\circ$ with $f(0)=p$. Its shadow is $df_0(\D)\subset T_pY$. In a local coordinate $z$ with $z(p)=0$, its radius is $r_z(D,p)=|(z\circ f)'(0)|$. Changing $f$ by a rotation changes neither the shadow nor its radius. Changing coordinate to $w$ multiplies the radius by $|dw/dz(p)|$.
notes: Pointed-disc parametrizations differ by a rotation; shadow is independent of that ambiguity.

statement: Let $f_\pm:(\D,0)\to(D_\pm,p_\pm)$ be pointed conformal parametrizations. An orientation-reversing isometry between their boundary circle torsors has the form $\zeta_- = e^{i\theta}/\zeta_+$ on $|\zeta_+|=1$. The induced propagator is \[ q=e^{i\theta}df_{+,0}(1)\otimes df_{-,0}(1) \in T_{p_+}Y\otimes T_{p_-}Y, \qquad |q|_{z_+,z_-}=r_{z_+}(D_+,p_+)r_{z_-}(D_-,p_-). \] The inverse tensor, viewed as a nonzero bilinear pairing into $\C$, has reciprocal modulus.
notes: Rotation covariance checked explicitly; tensor and dual pairing conventions separated.

statement: If $f:\D\hookrightarrow\PP^1\setminus\{1,\infty\}$ is holomorphic, $f(0)=0$, and $r=|f'(0)|$, then $r\leq4$.
notes: Opened Siu Koebe proof; normalized omitted value gives radius at most4.

statement: For the targets described on 67/075--078, the capping-and-forgetting maps $MD_{0,4}\to M_{\mathrm{st}}N_{0,4}$ and, whenever defined with the same unrestricted nodal tensor, $MDB_{0,4}\to M_{\mathrm{st}}ND_{0,4}$ are not surjective. In particular, they are not algebraic, complex analytic, real analytic, topological, or set-theoretic isomorphisms onto those targets. Lead L2 is false.
notes: Complete labelled stable(0,4) target with tensor17; each radius at most4, product at most16.

statement: Fix any stable pointed complex curve $Y$ with at least one node. The propagators obtainable from embedded caps on its fixed normalization are bounded in each nodal tangent line, for any fixed Hermitian norms. Thus the unrestricted nonzero-tensor target over $Y$ is never the image of capping. For every stable type with $3g-3+n>0$ this gives a counterexample to a global isomorphism. The sole stable type of complexity zero is $(0,3)$; there are no nodal stable curves of that type, and capping with all three external discs retained is an equivalence.
notes: Genus0 Koebe, genus1 area, genus>=2 Schwarz-Pick; finite automorphism ambiguity and (0,3),(1,1) retained.

statement: If the source on 67/074 includes arbitrary smooth cut circles, the canonical hyperbolic boundary torsors need not be respected by the identification of their two banks. In that interpretation the asserted pointed-disc anti-isomorphism, and hence the asserted tensor functor, is not defined by the stated construction. Restricting to geodesic cuts in the canonical hyperbolic metric removes this problem but does not remove Theorem~\ref{A:04}.
notes: Explicit analytic nonisometric welding t↦−t−epsilon sin(t); geodesic cuts repair torsor compatibility.

statement: For a fixed stable graph $\Gamma$, consider the following two groupoids: (i) hyperbolic bordered surfaces with labelled disjoint essential geodesic cuts of graph $\Gamma$, with conformal isomorphisms preserving all labels; (ii) their compact normalized components with a full admissible system of pointed cap discs at every half-edge and external mark, equal hyperbolic lengths on paired half-edges, and a specified orientation-reversing toric identification on each paired boundary. Cutting and capping gives an equivalence of these groupoids, with inverse obtained by deleting the node caps and welding the paired boundaries. Cuspidal external components are allowed as zero discs.
notes: Fully faithful and essentially surjective retained-cap groupoid equivalence; Fermi metric proves geodesic gluing.

statement: For a stable complex curve $Y$ and a multicurve $\Gamma$ representing its nodes, choose holomorphic coordinates $z_e,w_e$ near the two branches of each node and local parameters $u$ for the pointed normalization. For sufficiently small $t_e$, the equations $z_ew_e=t_e$ yield local analytic deformation coordinates after the appropriate Dehn-twist quotient. Their normal tangent directions are canonically the lines $T_{p_e^+}Y\otimes T_{p_e^-}Y$. This does not identify an entire product of punctured tangent lines with the global cut-surface moduli.
notes: Opened Hubbard–Koch Theorems9.11/10.1; local analytic chart is not a global inverse to forgotten caps.

statement: Let $S$ be a compact oriented surface with $n\geq1$ labelled boundary components and $\chi(S)=2-2g-n<0$. Let $\mathcal T^B(S)$ denote marked hyperbolic surfaces with these boundary components geodesic, and let $\mathcal T_{g,n}$ denote the Teichmuller space of the corresponding punctured surfaces. Canonical capping of 67/061--070, followed by remembering the cap centres, satisfies \[ \Psi=(\operatorname{cap},\ell):\mathcal T^B(S) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\mathcal T_{g,n}\times(0,\infty)^n \] as a mapping-class-equivariant real analytic diffeomorphism. Allowing some boundary lengths to vanish extends this to a homeomorphism \[ \overline\Psi:\mathcal T^{B,\geq0}(S) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\mathcal T_{g,n}\times[0,\infty)^n, \] real analytic on every fixed boundary/cusp stratum. No assertion of analyticity across all corner strata is needed here.
notes: Opened Mondello Theorem5.4; analytic fixed-positive-length stratum and continuous cusp-face extension are distinguished.

statement: For a marked compact Riemann surface $(X,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ with $2g-2+n>0$, the complete curvature $-1$ metric on $X\setminus\{p_i\}$ defines a canonical Hermitian norm on every $T_{p_i}X$. A normalized cusp coordinate $q$ has \[ ds^2=\frac{|dq|^2}{|q|^2(\log|q|)^2},\qquad \|\partial_q\|_{\mathrm{cusp}}=1. \] In its embedded range the horocycle $|q|=\rho$ has length $h=-2\pi/\log\rho$. The unrestricted horocycle-decoration torsor is parametrized by $h>0$, with no requirement that all projected horocycles be disjoint. Via $h_i=\ell_i$, Theorem~\ref{A:grafting} identifies the positive-length capping bundle with Penner's decoration bundle. This identification does not send actual cap shadows to cusp discs.
notes: Opened Wolpert cusp normalization and Penner decorations; exact h=−2pi/log rho formula; no disjointness assertion for arbitrary decorations.

statement: Let $(X,h)$ be a compact hyperbolic surface with geodesic boundary. Remove smooth open boundary collars so that the remaining surface $X'$ is diffeomorphic to $X$. Let $h'$ be its canonical hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary. There is a unique smooth real function $u$ on $X'$ such that $h'=e^{2u}h$, and it is characterized by \[ \Delta_hu=e^{2u}-1\quad\text{on }X',\qquad \partial_{n}u=-k_h\quad\text{on }\partial X'. \] Here $\Delta_h=\operatorname{div}_h\nabla$, $n$ is the outward unit normal, and $k_h$ is geodesic curvature measured toward the interior of $X'$. For collars cut at constant inward distance $a_i>0$ below their embedding widths, $k_h=-\tanh a_i$ on the corresponding new boundary and $u>0$ throughout $X'$. Thus $h'>h$ pointwise there.
notes: Equidistant inward collar: maximum-principle comparison with exact boundary curvature. Arbitrary collars treated by separate nonmonotonicity theorem.

statement: Let compact oriented bordered Riemann surfaces have finitely many paired boundary circles, and glue each pair by an orientation-reversing quasisymmetric homeomorphism, measured in analytic boundary coordinates. The topological quotient carries a conformal structure which restricts to the given structures on every interior, and its seams are quasicircles. It is unique under the identity on the pieces. More generally, for any given welding homeomorphisms, two realizations are conformally identical if one realization's seams are conformally removable. Rectifiable seams satisfy this uniqueness condition. Quasisymmetry is sufficient for existence and characterizes quasicircle realizations; it is not necessary for existence of arbitrary Jordan-curve weldings.
notes: Opened Hamilton proof and Younsi removability discussion; QS existence and removable-seam uniqueness separately verified.

statement: Let $V$ be a Jordan disc and let $I$ be a Jordan arc with one endpoint on $\partial V$ and its remaining points in $V$. Cutting $V$ along $I$ gives a simply connected surface with a prime-end boundary circle. Its Riemann map has the boundary identifications of 67/071--073, with the slit tip and its two access points at the attachment prescribed as the three normalization points. No rectifiability is needed for this cutting assertion. Conversely, let the two designated boundary banks be identified by $\varphi$, and form their bank-exchanging involution $H$: $H=\varphi$ on one bank and $H=\varphi^{-1}$ on the other. Require $H$ to be quasisymmetric in an analytic boundary coordinate on the \emph{union} of the banks, including their common endpoint. This condition has a slit realization which is the image of a straight radial slit under a quasiconformal homeomorphism of a disc. After putting its tip at $0$ and its attachment at $1$ in the unit disc, the normalized realization is unique. Conversely every such quasiconformal slit pair has this welding condition. The correspondence is therefore with this specified class of slit pairs; quasisymmetry on a single bank alone is insufficient at the fold. For a prescribed rectifiable slit the normalized welding is unique, but ``rectifiable graph'' does not supply an existence criterion for an arbitrary interval homeomorphism.
notes: Opened Lind Lemma6; whole-bank QS includes endpoint distance comparability, necessary for slit extension.

statement: The interval homeomorphism $h(t)=t^2$ on $[0,1]$ is quasisymmetric, whereas the decreasing involution \[ H(x)=\begin{cases}-x^2&x\geq0,\\\sqrt{-x}&x\leq0\end{cases} \quad(-1\leq x\leq1) \] is not. For equal adjacent intervals at $0$, the ratio of the image lengths is $t^{1/2}/t^2=t^{-3/2}$, unbounded as $t\downarrow0$. To check the first assertion directly, for $t>0$ and $x\geq t$ the adjacent-increment ratio for $h$ is $(2x+t)/(2x-t)\in[1,3]$; the usual interval definition only tests triples in $[0,1]$. Thus the datum is quasisymmetric on one bank but cannot be the welding of a quasiconformal slit pair. We make no assertion here that it has no Jordan-slit realization in a larger class.
notes: Single-bank t^2 is QS but full folded map has unbounded adjacent ratio; explicit complete counterexample.

statement: On 67/074--082, geodesic cuts and the rotational capping identifications are real analytic, hence quasisymmetric and removable. No earlier assertion about arbitrary rectifiable weldings is needed for that construction. If ``differentiable cut'' is taken literally without toric compatibility, the obstruction in Proposition~\ref{A:arbitrarycuts} remains; smoothness alone does not produce the claimed nodal tensor.
notes: From074 onward smooth seams; no appeal to arbitrary rectifiable welding existence is needed.

statement: The model proposed on 67/019--020, in which all admissible pants caps are concentric subdiscs of three fixed orange slices, is false. There is a hyperbolic pair of pants with two cusps and third boundary length $32$ whose canonical cap cannot lie in the proposed cell at $0$.
notes: Hua-project extremal-length method credited; explicit annulus, exact inequality and corrected implicit length/radius parametrization.

statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a connected stable graph of type $(g,n)$, with edge set $E\ne\varnothing$. Fix its pointed compact normalization components $X_v$, with every branch and external marking labelled. For an ordinary fibre, retain an identification of the normalization with these fixed objects; merely labelling the special points need not remove their finite automorphisms. All constructions below are equivariant for those automorphisms and also define the corresponding groupoid maps. We first take all external ends to be cusps. At each special point choose a local coordinate, used only to measure radii and tensor moduli. Let $I_v$ be the set of node branches on $X_v$. For $a\in[0,\infty)^E$, define $(B_va)_h=a_e$ when the branch $h$ belongs to the edge $e$; both branches of a loop are included separately. Let $H_v$ be the Jenkins--Strebel support function for these active points, with all other special points kept marked, and put \[ H_\Gamma(a)=\sum_v H_v(B_va),\qquad H_v(0)=0. \] Define the explicit open convex set \[ K_\Gamma=\left\{y\in\R^E: \sum_e a_e y_e<H_\Gamma(a) \text{ for every }a\geq0,\ \sum_ea_e=1\right\}. \] The attainable nonzero node tensors are exactly those with $(\log|q_e|)_e\in K_\Gamma$. Every such tensor system has a unique labelled geodesic-cut preimage, up to the equivalence of Theorem~\ref{A:fullcaps}. More precisely, if $x_e=(\ell_e/2\pi)^2$, the logarithmic modulus map is \[ G_\Gamma(x)=\sum_v B_v^T F_v(B_vx),\qquad G_\Gamma:(0,\infty)^E\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K_\Gamma, \] where $F_v$ is the vector of logarithmic cap radii on $X_v$. It is a real analytic diffeomorphism with symmetric positive definite derivative. In the phase coordinates specified by normalized cap maps, the complete tangent map is block diagonal with blocks $DG_\Gamma$ and the identity on $\R^E$. This is the tangent map on the fixed normalization fibre. When the normalization components also vary, the differential is block triangular with the identity on the normalization-moduli base and this invertible fibre block. In particular the full real tangent map is invertible everywhere on the fixed graph stratum.
notes: SPD weighted radius Jacobian, support inequality, properness, and all normalization strata. Independent agent algebra_c audit passed.

statement: For a fixed labelled normalization with its identification retained, the map on ordinary fundamental groups from the geodesic-cut source to the unrestricted tensor target is the identity $\Z^E\to\Z^E$ in the twist generators, although its image is the proper domain of Theorem~\ref{A:graph-radius-domain}. The analogous statement holds for orbifold fundamental groups when the normalization components vary and their finite automorphisms are retained: inclusion of the restricted tensor domain is a homotopy equivalence on each fixed graph stratum. This is compatible with the everywhere invertible real tangent map. Neither test supplies the missing properness onto the unrestricted target.
notes: Fixed normalization fibre Z^E; identity phase map; convex logarithmic radius deformation. Orbifold and fully marked lift conventions explicit.

statement: Take the two labelled three-pointed spheres used in Theorem~\ref{A:04}, with all four external ends cuspidal. Each node cap has the same radius $r(\lambda)$, which increases strictly from $0$ to $4$ as $\lambda$ increases from $0$ to infinity. The precise tensor image in the specified coordinates is \[ 0<|q|<16. \] The parameter relation is $|q|=r(\lambda)^2$ and its phase is the boundary twist. Thus this fibre is a punctured disc, whereas the proposed unrestricted target fibre is $\C^*$. The derivative never vanishes and both fundamental groups are $\Z$, with degree one map.
notes: Full corrected fixed normalization fibre0<|q|<16; strict monotonicity and JS endpoint4.

statement: The same finite-dimensional inversion determines the image when external caps are retained. Add one positive variable $x_i$ for each positive external boundary, and one output coordinate $\log r_i$ for its shadow. In $B_v$, copy a node variable to each of its two flags and an external variable to its single flag. Then $B^T(F_v)_v$ is a real analytic diffeomorphism onto the strict support domain with support $\sum_vH_v(B_va)$. For specified normalization components, node tensors, and actual external pointed discs, the following is a necessary and sufficient test for a geodesic-cut preimage: their tensor moduli and external shadow radii belong to that domain; the unique recovered length vector produces exactly the specified external discs. When both conditions hold, the preimage is unique. Zero external radii are handled on their corresponding face. This test states the additional disc compatibility instead of assuming that forgetting node caps preserves admissibility.
notes: Includes external flags, then tests equality of the actual retained external discs. Does not replace that compatibility by radius alone.

statement: The inverse on the restricted propagator domain in Theorem~\ref{A:graph-radius-domain} is a plumbing in the canonical cap coordinates, which themselves depend on the recovered length vector. If $z_\pm$ are coordinates at the two node branches and $f_\pm:\D\to D_\pm$ are normalized so that $(z_\pm\circ f_\pm)'(0)=r_\pm>0$, put $Z_\pm=r_\pm f_\pm^{-1}$. Its seam identification is exactly \[ Z_+Z_-=q,\qquad q=r_+r_-e^{i\theta}. \] This identity does not identify the radius inverse with plumbing in one fixed pair of coordinate germs for all $q$.
notes: Normalized cap coordinates give exact moving-coordinate equation Z+Z−=q. Algebra_c independent audit passed.
